constructionSummary: Two matched arms, differing ONLY in the hidden graded scenario set's sessionsBetween value (0 vs 3). Visible package files (README.md, SPEC.md, types.ts, starter/subject.mjs, examples/) are produced by buildMemoryChallengePackage unmodified for both arms and are byte-identical apart from MANIFEST.json's scenarioSetId. Mechanically confirmed via requireMatchedPair (src/phase-21/matched-pair.ts): sharedComponentsConfirmed = [enumerateSpace/generateScenarios/buildScenario, verify (via runCell), reference, mutants, visible package construction]; differingFields = [scenarios.params.sessionsBetween] only.

validityGate.note: same-session-resolver is not caught at sessionsBetween=0 — expected and documented in the family's own scenarios.ts comment: at 0 the ingest and act share one session by construction, so a same-session-resolving strategy is indistinguishable from correct behavior there. Caught at the treated arm instead (see below); jointly, every mutant is caught by at least one arm.

visible-origin-attributor is not caught at sessionsBetween=3 — its discriminative signal is apparently session-boundary-dependent in the opposite direction from same-session-resolver. Caught at the baseline arm instead; jointly, every mutant is caught by at least one arm.

arms.jointValidityCriterion: reference clean in BOTH arms (true), AND every one of the 13 mutants caught by AT LEAST ONE arm (true — verified: same-session-resolver only at treated, visible-origin-attributor only at baseline, all 11 others at both). This is the correct validity bar for a parameter-value matched pair: requiring EVERY mutant to fire identically in BOTH single-value arms would be the wrong bar, since some mutants' defects are inherently session-boundary-dependent by the family's own design (documented in scenarios.ts) — that dependence is real signal about the mechanism, not a validity failure.

design.initialCommitment: 2 attempts per provider (OpenAI, Anthropic) per arm — 4 attempts per arm, 8 total initial attempts, forming 4 genuine matched pairs (by provider + attempt-index) across the two arms.
design.conditionalExpansion: to 8 matched pairs (16 total attempts: 8 per arm, 4 per provider per arm) under the preregistered directional stopping rule below, evaluated via evaluateStoppingRule exactly as Phase 14 and Phase 21 both already do.
design.armOrderRandomization: Randomize which arm (baseline or treated) each attempt slot receives first, per provider, so ordering cannot correlate with model version drift or time-of-day effects.
design.identicalSettings: Same model, effort, isolation (cell-container — prompt-injection-memory-poisoning is already migrated), and timeout across both arms; only the package (and therefore the hidden scenario set) differs.
design.blindAdjudication: Every failure is independently, blindly cross-provider-adjudicated before counting as capability evidence, reusing Phase 14's established two-reader pattern (src/phase-14/measurement.ts) — not a new adjudication scheme.
design.outcomeMetric: Per matched pair (same provider, same attempt index): baseline=1 if the real submission solves the baseline package cleanly (reward 1, no failed checks across its graded scenarios), treated=1 under the same criterion for the treated package. Fed into mcNemarExact/evaluateStoppingRule exactly as src/phase-22/orchestrator.ts already does for its own matched observations — reused, not reinvented.
design.evidenceCategory: fresh-trusted-agent-difficulty — a NEW category, distinct from mutant-coverage (Lane 3's validity gates, which are validity checks not hardness evidence) and from regraded-real-submission (Phase 22's category, which reuses PRESERVED submissions rather than running new ones). Never to be combined with either.

authorizationStatus: NOT AUTHORIZED as of this preregistration. This design is frozen and trial-ready; executing it requires separate, explicit, in-the-moment operator authorization to spend real provider money on real agent attempts, which this document cannot itself grant.
